Each of the at least one pyrolysis zone, the cooling zone, and the preheating zone (if present) may be located within a single unit, or in separate units. The material feed system may be physically integrated with the BPU. In some embodiments, the cooler is disposed within the BPU. The system may further include one or more additive feeders for introducing additive(s) into the system, such as any of the above-described additives. In some embodiments, an additive feeder is configured to combine the additive with the carbon-containing feedstock. An additive feeder may be interposed between the material feed system (for biomass) and the BPU. An additive feeder may be disposed in operable communication with the BPU. An additive feeder may be disposed in operable communication with the cooler. An additive feeder may be interposed between the cooler and the carbon recovery unit. An additive feeder may disposed in operable communication with the carbon recovery unit, including downstream of the recovery unit itself. The BPU may be configured with a first gas inlet and a first gas outlet. The first gas inlet and the first gas outlet may be disposed in communication with different zones, or the same zone. In various embodiments, the BPU is configured with any one or more of a second gas inlet, a second gas outlet, a third gas inlet, a third gas outlet, a fourth gas inlet, and a fourth gas outlet. Optionally, each zone present in the BPU is configured with a gas inlet and a gas outlet. Gas inlets and outlets allow not only introduction and withdrawal of vapor or gas, but also allow precise process monitoring and control across various stages of the process, resulting in yield and efficiency improvements. In some embodiments, the cooling zone is configured with a gas inlet, and the pyrolysis zone is configured with a gas outlet, to generate substantially countercurrent flow of the gas phase relative to the solid phase (e.g., the feedstock). In other embodiments, the cooling zone is configured with a gas inlet, and the preheating zone is configured with a gas outlet, to generate substantially countercurrent flow of the gas phase relative to the solid phase. In these or other embodiments, the cooling zone is configured with a gas inlet, and the drying zone is configured with a gas outlet, to generate substantially countercurrent flow of the gas phase relative to the solid phase. The system may further comprise a first reaction gas probe disposed in operable communication with the pyrolysis zone and with a gas-monitoring device, such as (but not limited to) GC, MS, GC-MS, or FTIR. In some embodiments, the system further comprises a second reaction gas probe disposed in operable communication with the cooling zone and with the gas-monitoring device or a second gas-monitoring device which may be a different type of instrument. The system may include additional reaction gas probes disposed in operable communication with the drying zone (if present) and/or the preheating zone (if present), and with a gas-monitoring device. When reaction gas probes are included, the system may further include at least one computer-programmed controller executable to utilize output from the gas-monitoring device to adjust a system set point (such as pyrolysis temperature or inert gas flow rate). In some embodiments, the system further comprises a process gas heater disposed in operable communication with the outlet to remove condensable vapors and non-condensable gases, wherein the process gas heater is configured to introduce a separate fuel and an oxidant into a combustion chamber, adapted for combustion of the fuel and at least a portion of the condensable vapors. The system may include a heat exchanger disposed between the process gas heater and the dryer, configured to utilize at least some of the heat of the combustion for the dryer. Alternatively, or additionally, the system may include a heat exchanger disposed between the process gas heater and a gas inlet for the BPU, configured to utilize at least some of the heat of the combustion for preheating a substantially inert gas prior to introduction into the BPU. In some embodiments, the system further comprises a carbon-enrichment unit, disposed in operable communication with the cooler or the BPU, configured for combining vapors, including noncondensable vapors and/or condensable vapors in fully or at least partially condensed form, with the solids to increase the carbon content of the high-carbon biogenic reagent obtained from the carbon recovery unit. In various embodiments, the system is configured for extracting and reusing gases from the BPU and/or extracting and reusing gases from the carbon recovery unit. In some embodiments, the system further comprises a separate pyrolysis unit adapted to further pyrolyze the high-carbon biogenic reagent to further increase its carbon content. Other variations provide a high-carbon biogenic reagent production system, the system comprising: This system may include a deaerater disposed between the material feed system or the dryer (if present) and the preheater. The system may be configured with at least two gas inlets and at least two gas outlets, if desired. In some embodiments, the pyrolysis reactor and/or the cooler is configured with gas inlet(s), and the dryer (if present) and/or the preheater is configured with gas outlet(s), to generate substantially countercurrent flow of the gas phase relative to the solid phase. The system further includes a process gas heater, in some embodiments, disposed in operable communication with the at least one gas outlet to remove condensable vapors and non-condensable gases. The process gas heater can be configured to introduce a separate fuel and an oxidant into a combustion chamber, adapted for combustion of the fuel and at least a portion of the condensable vapors. The system may include a heat exchanger disposed between the process gas heater and the dryer, configured to utilize at least some of the heat of the combustion for the dryer. The system may include a heat exchanger disposed between the process gas heater and a gas inlet for the BPU, configured to utilize at least some of the heat of the combustion for preheating a substantially inert gas prior to introduction into the pyrolysis reactor. Certain variations provide a biomass-pyrolysis continuous reactor comprising a feedstock inlet, a plurality of spatially separated reactors configured for separately controlling the temperature and mixing within each of the reactors, and a carbonaceous-solids outlet, wherein one of the reactors is configured with a first gas inlet for introducing a substantially inert gas into the reactor, and wherein one of the reactors is configured with a first gas outlet. In some embodiments, the BPU includes at least two, three, or four zones. Each of the zones may be disposed in communication with separately adjustable indirect heating means, each independently selected from the group consisting of electrical heat transfer, steam heat transfer, hot-oil heat transfer, waste-heat transfer, and combinations thereof. The BPU may be configured for separately adjusting gas-phase composition and gas-phase residence time of at least two zones. In some embodiments, the BPU is configured for separately adjusting gas-phase composition and gas-phase residence time of all zones present in the BPU. In some embodiments, the BPU is configured with a second gas inlet and/or a second gas outlet. In certain embodiments, the BPU is configured with a gas inlet in each zone and/or a gas outlet in each zone. In some embodiments, the BPU is a countercurrent reactor. The material feed system may comprise a feed mechanism selected from the group consisting of a screw, an auger, a drop chamber, and a drum material feed system. The carbonaceous-solids outlet may comprise an output mechanism selected from the group consisting of a screw, an auger, a drop chamber, and a drum material feed system. The BPU may include a single auger disposed throughout each of the zones. In some embodiments, each of the reactors is configured with flights disposed on internal walls, to provide agitation of solids. The flights may be separately adjustable in each of the zones. The BPU is an axially rotatable BPU, in some embodiments. Still other variations of the invention provide a process for producing a high-carbon biogenic reagent, the process comprising: In some embodiments, step (h) includes passing at least a portion of the condensable vapors from step (e), in vapor and/or condensed form, across the warm pyrolyzed solids, to produce enriched pyrolyzed solids with increased carbon and/or energy content. In these or other embodiments, step (h) includes passing at least a portion of the non-condensable gases from step (e) across the warm pyrolyzed solids, to produce enriched pyrolyzed solids with increased carbon and/or energy content. In some embodiments, step (h) includes passing at least a portion of the condensable vapors from step (e), in vapor and/or condensed form, across the cool pyrolyzed solids, to produce enriched pyrolyzed solids with increased carbon and/or energy content. In these or other embodiments, step (h) includes passing at least a portion of the non-condensable gases from step (e) across the cool pyrolyzed solids, to produce enriched pyrolyzed solids with increased carbon and/or energy content. In certain embodiments, step (h) includes passing substantially all of the condensable vapors from step (e), in vapor and/or condensed form, across the cool pyrolyzed solids, to produce enriched pyrolyzed solids with increased carbon and/or energy content. In these or other embodiments, step (h) includes passing substantially all of the non-condensable gases from step (e) across the cool pyrolyzed solids, to produce enriched pyrolyzed solids with increased carbon content. Energy may be recovered from the condensable vapors, the non-condensable gases, or both, for use in the process. Energy may be recovered through heat exchange with these streams. Optionally, either or both of the condensable vapors and non-condensable gases may be combusted, and the heat of combustion may be recovered for process use. The process may further include introducing an intermediate feed stream consisting of at least a portion of the condensable vapors and at least a portion of the non-condensable gases, obtained from step (e), to a separation unit configured to generate at least first and second output streams. The intermediate feed stream may include all of the condensable vapors and/or all of the non-condensable gases, in certain embodiments. A portion of the second output stream may be recycled to step (d) for use as substantially inert gas in the pyrolysis unit, alone or in combination with another source of inert gas (e.g., N 2 ). The first and second output streams may be separated based on relative volatility, for example. In some embodiments, the first output stream comprises the condensable vapors (e.g., terpenes, alcohols, acids, aldehydes, or ketones), and the second output stream comprises the non-condensable gases (e.g., carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and methane). The first and second output streams may be separated based on relative polarity. In these embodiments, the first output stream comprises polar compounds (e.g., methanol, furfural, and acetic acid), and the second output stream comprises non-polar compounds (e.g., carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, methane, terpenes, and terpene derivatives). In some embodiments, step (h) increases the total carbon content, fixed carbon content, and/or energy content of the high-carbon biogenic reagent, relative to an otherwise-identical process without step (h). In some embodiments, step (h) increases the fixed carbon content of the high-carbon biogenic reagent, relative to an otherwise-identical process without step (h). This invention also provides a continuous or batch process for increasing carbon and/or energy content of any carbon-containing material. In some variations, a process for producing a high-carbon biogenic reagent comprises: In some embodiments, the starting carbon-containing material is pyrolyzed biomass or torrefied biomass. The gas stream may be obtained during an integrated process that provides the carbon-containing material. Or, the gas stream may be obtained from separate processing of the carbon-containing material. The gas stream, or a portion thereof, may be obtained from an external source. Mixtures of gas streams, as well as mixtures of carbon-containing materials, from a variety of sources, are possible. In some embodiments, the process further comprises recycling or reusing the gas stream for repeating the process to further increase carbon and/or energy content of the carbon-containing product. In some embodiments, the process further comprises recycling or reusing the gas stream for carrying out the process to increase carbon and/or energy content of another feedstock different from the carbon-containing material. This process may include introducing the gas stream to a separation unit configured to generate at least first and second output streams, wherein the gas stream comprises a mixture of condensable carbon-containing vapors and non-condensable carbon-containing gases. The first and second output streams may be separated based on relative volatility or relative polarity, for example. In some embodiments, the carbon-containing product has higher total carbon content and/or fixed carbon content and/or volatile carbon content than the carbon-containing material. In some embodiments, the carbon-containing product has higher energy content than the carbon-containing material. A high-carbon biogenic reagent production system is also provided, the system comprising: In some embodiments, the system further comprises a preheating zone, disposed in operable communication with the pyrolysis zone. Each of the pyrolysis zone, the cooling zone, and the preheating zone (if present) may be located within a single unit, or in separate units. The dryer, if present, may be configured as a drying zone within the BPU.

title: Harmless treatment method for oil sludge pyrolysis
text: Harmless treatment method for oil sludge pyrolysis The invention relates to a harmless treatment method for oil sludge pyrolysis, comprising the following steps: oil sludge pretreatment; oil sludge pyrolysis; pyrolysis oil and gas separation; pyrolysis residue decarbonization and heat carrier regeneration. According to the method, the sludge is preliminarily treated and then enters a pyrolyzer, and undergoes mild pyrolysis under the action of a heat carrier; after pyrolysis, oil and gas are condensed and separated to obtain pyrolysis oil and pyrolysis gas. After the pyrolysis slag and heat carrier are regenerated by combustion and decarbonization, a part is returned to the pyrolyzer for recycling, and the pyrolysis gas is burned to provide heat for the heat carrier and remove carbon deposits on the pyrolysis slag. In the method, the oil in the sludge can be recovered by pyrolysis of the sludge. After the pyrolysis, the sludge is converted into a carbon-containing pyrolysis residue and then burned, thereby avoiding the generation of dioxins in the direct combustion of the sludge, and at the same time recovering the oil in the sludge. The invention reasonably utilizes the gas, waste heat, etc. produced by pyrolysis, and realizes the harmless and resource utilization of oil sludge. So that environmental benefits, social benefits and economic benefits are concentrated. The invention relates to a harmless treatment method for oil sludge pyrolysis. More specifically, the processing method and the process thereof are used for pyrolyzing the oil sludge under the action of a heat carrier to obtain oil products and pyrolysis gas, and combusting the carbon deposition pyrolysis slag, thereby realizing resource utilization and harmless treatment of dangerous solid wastes. The oily sludge is mainly composed of oil, mud and water. The oil stain contains a large amount of odorous toxic substances such as benzene series, phenols, anthracene, pyrene and the like, and if the oil stain is not properly treated, the oil stain can pollute water, soil and the like and cause environmental pollution. The national hazardous waste list is listed in HW08, and relates to the industries of oil extraction, natural gas extraction and refined oil product manufacture. The oily sludge, especially the high-oil sludge, is organically collected, and an economical and practical method is developed and researched for carrying out harmless treatment and sump oil recovery on the oily sludge, so that a large amount of energy can be recovered, certain economic benefit is generated, pollution is reduced, and huge environmental benefit and social benefit are generated. At present, the domestic oily sludge resource recovery technology mainly comprises the following steps: solvent extraction technology, hot water washing treatment technology, biological treatment technology, profile control technology, thermal extraction-dehydration treatment technology, ultrasonic deoiling technology, oil sludge incineration and other methods. The incineration is obvious in reduction, harmless and thorough, and resource utilization can be realized, but the oil sludge contains certain heavy metals and organic matters, secondary pollution is caused by incineration, and the problem of dioxin is particularly serious; the biological treatment method is to degrade oil-containing sludge by using microorganisms under certain conditions, but the degradation period is long, the difficulty in the interpretation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in the oil sludge is high, the biological treatment method is only suitable for the oil sludge with the oil content of less than 5 percent, the occupied area is large, and the treatment difficulty is increased along with the increase of the water content of the oil sludge; the hot washing method only carries out simple oil-sludge separation, the treatment cost mainly depends on the price of a medicament, the quality of the treatment effect has a direct relation with the aging degree of oil products and the dosage of the medicament, the product value is not high, and the treatment of reduction and recycling is difficult to achieve; the distribution coefficient of the solvent extraction method, the separation effect of the extraction liquid from water and mud, the regeneration effect of the extractant, the loss rate of the extractant and the like are difficult to control. The pyrolysis method has thorough reduction, stabilization and harmless treatment capacity, realizes resource utilization of the oil sludge, is more advanced compared with the incineration method, eliminates dangerous waste, avoids secondary pollution, avoids the generation of dioxin through anaerobic pyrolysis, and is one of the most promising and environment-friendly methods for treating the oil sludge at present. The foreign treatment modes of the oil sludge mainly comprise pyrolysis and gasification treatment. For example, canadian patent CA2907624A provides an externally heated rotary retort for the pyrolysis of oil sands, oil sludge (e.g., crude oil and soil mixtures, tank bottom sludge, refinery sludge), oil shale, and biomass to produce high purity, low cost products. The problem of wall sticking of the solid material in the pyrolysis process is effectively solved by regulating and controlling the return material. US patent US 10294427 provides a catalytic fast pyrolysis (RCFP) process at low pressure by pyrolyzing biomass, sludge, etc. under the action of hydrogen, pyrolysis gas and a catalyst to obtain a light oil. International patent WO/2009/020442 provides a system for gasifying solids such as coal, lignite, petroleum coke, hazardous solid waste, domestic solid waste, industrial solid waste, biomass, etc. The gasification furnace comprises: a drying zone, a pyrolysis zone, a first gasification zone (an oxidation zone and a reduction zone), an isolation shielding zone, a screen zone, a second oxidation zone and the like. In addition, the system includes an ash, a water cooling system, and a gas cleanup discharge system. US patent US14566914 provides a process and associated equipment for producing industrially useful products from used hydrocarbon-containing materials such as rubber, plastics and municipal waste. The hydrocarbon-containing waste is subjected to anaerobic pyrolysis in the presence of a zeolite-type catalyst. Gaseous and liquid hydrocarbons are produced in the process, and the process can increase the liquid hydrocarbon yield. The gaseous and liquid products are typically further used by combustion to provide heat for pyrolysis or to generate electricity. US10533415 provides a multistage process for the treatment of organic waste comprising drying the organic waste to reduce the water content thereof to below 15%; the dried waste is subjected to a thermal extraction treatment at a temperature of about 275 â to 375 â and in the presence of a circulating solvent medium of up to 10 atmospheres to obtain gaseous, liquid and solid products; the slurry product obtained by the thermal extraction is transferred to a pyrolysis device and is further pyrolyzed at a temperature of 350 â to 500 â. The pyrolysis oil gas is further subjected to condensation separation and vacuum distillation to obtain oil products and gas. U.S. Pat. No. 4,11425347, International patent PCT/US2006/024018, provides systems and methods for the thermal conversion of sludge into fuel. The system consists of a reaction module, 1-2 condensation modules, a combustion module, a separation module and a control valve. The sludge is heated and converted into pyrolysis steam and carbon residue in an oxygen-free environment by the process, the pyrolysis steam takes bio-oil as a cold medium at the temperature higher than the boiling point of water, the bio-oil is separated by a spray condenser to obtain bio-oil, and the non-condensable gas enters a combustion system for combustion and heat supply. The process has the advantages that the gas-liquid separation temperature is higher than 100 â, and no condensed water is generated. US patent No. 15438948 provides an apparatus and process for producing synthesis gas from organic solid fuel for use in internal combustion engines, comprising feeding pyrolysis feedstock such as sewage sludge, pulp and scum from the bottom of a pyrolysis reactor into a fluidized bed reactor. The synthesis gas produced in the fluidized bed reactor is withdrawn as product gas. The product gas is directly or indirectly supplied to the internal combustion engine. Japanese patent of invention JP1996990 proposes a technique for producing low viscosity oils and gases by drying sludge and transferring it from a hopper to a reactor tube for pyrolysis. The reaction tube is externally provided with an electric furnace, and pyrolysis is carried out at the temperature of 200-600 â without oxygen to obtain carbon and low-viscosity oil products. The pyrolysis oil gas is separated into high boiling point oil products through first condensation and returns to the reaction tube, and the high boiling point oil products are continuously cracked into small molecules through the catalytic action of carbon deposition on the pyrolysis slag. And further condensing and separating the primarily separated condensed oil gas to obtain gas and low-viscosity oil products. US10997334 proposes the conversion of organic waste materials such as municipal waste, sewage and biomass into synthesis gas. The technique employs a moving bed reactor. The solid material falls into the reactor from the upper part and descends by gravity, the ash slag is discharged from the bottom, and hot flue gas generated by the combustion furnace enters the lower part of the reactor for heat supply. The reactor is provided with quenching water to regulate the reaction intensity. And part of the generated synthesis gas enters a combustion furnace to be combusted for heat supply. Italian patent IT10859318 proposes that organic solid waste, sludge, black liquid and the like are mixed with oil to be in a flowable state, the mixture is sent into a container, then the mixture enters a heated evaporator through a pipeline to be pyrolyzed, part of pyrolysis steam (oil + gas) enters a combustor to be combusted to supply heat for the evaporator, and part of oil is recycled to be mixed with solid raw materials for use or used as a product. US14675223 provides a process for producing diesel and jet fuel from renewable feedstocks. The technology introduces renewable resources such as vegetable oils, corn, rapeseed, canola, soybean and algal oils, animal fats, oils and fats, sewage sludge, and the like into a hydrogenation and deoxygenation zone and separates hydrocarbon emissions from the hydrogenation and deoxygenation zone into an aviation kerosene fraction and a diesel fraction. US20160194568, WO/2015/007285 provide an apparatus and a method for gasification in a circulating fluidized bed reactor, which converts grain stalks, straw, municipal and industrial organic wastes, sewage sludge and the like into synthesis gas using a circulating fluidized bed gasification apparatus. The circulating fluidized bed reactor includes a single pyrolysis reaction chamber, one or more primary coke gasification chambers, and one or more secondary coke gasification chambers. US patent US20100147670 proposes a thermal decomposition method and apparatus. The device has horizontal stirring facilities, and the horizontal shaft has electric heating to supply heat for the pyrolysis process. Meat and bone meal, oil sludge and the like are thermally decomposed into pyrolysis oil gas and residues in the device, and the pyrolysis oil gas is further condensed and separated to obtain pyrolysis oil and pyrolysis gas. Therefore, foreign patents for the treatment of oil sludge mainly refer to pyrolysis equipment, gasification treatment process and equipment, or a process for producing high-quality oil products through hydrotreating. The pyrolysis process may add a catalyst or solvent. And these pyrolysis or gasification patents have no concern as to whether the treated sludge will be treated to render it harmless for hazardous solid waste. Related patents aiming at oil sludge pyrolysis in China are more, for example, in a patent CN108178477 oil-containing sludge recovery processing system in an oil field, oil sludge is added into a heating spiral pre-demulsification device to separate oil, water and solid, and the solid enters a rotary pyrolysis system for anaerobic pyrolysis. A pre-treatment is required to separate a portion of the oil and water prior to pyrolysis. Patent CN109133560 is a process for recycling oil sludge, which directly prepares oil sludge with water content more than 40% or prepares oil sludge with water, and then separates oil and water by stirring, heating, air flotation, aeration, ultrasonic separation and the like to obtain solid oil sludge. And (4) pyrolyzing the oil sludge. The pyrolysis slag is incinerated, and flocculating agents, polymers and the like are added in the process, so that pollution is increased. Patent CN20498153 a system that makes oily sludge innocent treatment, add the medicament with fatlute and wash the branch oil, the solid carries out the pyrolysis in the rotary kiln after the separation, and the pyrolysis is gone on under oxidizing atmosphere, and the pyrolysis sediment is directly discharged. The process does not consider the problem of metal residue in the oil sludge, and the solid waste is not completely treated. The addition of chemicals and water increases pollution. In the patent CN105399294, oil sludge is crushed and added with an alkaline agent and a demulsifier to separate oil and water, the dried oil sludge is added with a pyrolysis catalyst (5 percent) to carry out pyrolysis with the flue gas of a hot blast stove by indirect heat exchange (600 plus 800 â) so as to recover part of oil products, and the oil content of the pyrolysis residue is less than 0.3 percent. In the process of treating the oil sludge by the method, an alkaline medicament, a demulsifier and a catalyst are added, so that other pollutants in the pyrolytic slag are increased while the oil sludge is treated, only oil products in the oil sludge are removed, and the pyrolytic slag is not treated. The patent CN105399294 oil sludge recycling and harmless treatment process. Adding alkaline agent and demulsifier into oil sludge, hot washing, separating, and drying oil sludge containing 2-8% oil and 50-70% water. And adding 5% of pyrolysis catalyst into the dried oil sludge for pyrolysis. The solid waste amount is increased by adding the catalyst in the process, and the catalyst is difficult to separate from the pyrolysis residue. Patent CN106219940 discloses a process for treating oil-containing sludge by using hot steam, in which oil sludge is dehydrated after adding a demulsifier, and dried oil sludge is pyrolyzed by using supersonic high-temperature steam and adding a catalyst. The addition of catalyst in the process increases the solid waste amount, and supersonic high-temperature steam is not easy to obtain. Patent CN10669888 is a fatlute resourceful treatment system, adopts the pyrolyzer of special structure to carry out the pyrolysis to fatlute. The patent mainly carries out treatments such as alkali liquor washing, water washing, multi-medium catalytic oxidation and the like on pyrolysis gas, and pyrolysis slag is not further treated. The addition of alkali washing and water washing in the process increases pollutants and wastes water resources. Patent CN106957136 discloses a method for treating oily sludge. The sludge is separated and dehydrated after being added with the medicament, and is pyrolyzed and carbonized after being dried, the pyrolysis generates high temperature through a side hot blast stove in indirect heat supply, and the high temperature is heated and decomposed in a micro-oxygen or anaerobic state. The slag after pyrolysis contains less than 1% water. In the process, 1-20% of medicament is required to be added into the oil sludge in advance for dehydration and deoiling. Patent CN106746419 is an industrial scale pyrolysis treatment system and method for oil-containing sludge, which is to pre-sort and screen the oil sludge, add medicament, and carry out hot water centrifugal solid-liquid separation to obtain solid with oil content less than 5% and water content less than 80%. Dried and pyrolyzed. The process has complicated pyrolytic pretreatment process, and needs adding medicaments, crushing, sieving and the like. Patent CN107327851 hazardous waste incineration system is cooperated with a method for disposing complex sludge. Lime powder is added into the oil sludge for homogenization, then the oil sludge is combusted for heat supply, and the heat of combustion is recycled. Patent CN206279174 sled dress formula oil sludge pyrolysis treatment system comprises stoving pyrolysis sled piece, oil gas water separation sled piece, fluidized bed gasification sled piece. Drying the oil sludge, gasifying the pyrolyzed slag and the pyrolyzed oil in a fluidized bed to generate coal gas, and burning the gasified coal gas in a waste heat boiler to supply heat. In the process, the direct combustion of the oil sludge is converted into the gasification combustion after pyrolysis, so that the generation of dioxin is avoided to a certain extent, but the process is complex. Patent CN207483591 a mud, fatlute composite pyrolysis system adopts the composite pyrolysis stove to use hot flue gas to be the heat source respectively to fatlute and pyrolysis oil pyrolysis for the gas, and the gas is burnt in the flue gas generating furnace and is produced the heat supply of high temperature flue gas. Directly discharging the pyrolysis slag. Patent CN108455807 is an oily sludge innocent treatment device and method, adopting a circulating hot air external heating U-shaped pyrolyzing furnace to pyrolyze oil sludge, and condensing and separating pyrolysis products. The non-condensable gas and the pyrolysis oil enter a combustion furnace for combustion and heat supply. The pyrolysis slag is discharged as general solid waste, and the flue gas adopts ultraviolet rays generated by a UV generator, strong oxidizing active particles such as low-temperature plasma, ozone, hydroxyl free radicals and the like, and malodorous components (mainly organic acid, alcohol and ether) in the tail gas to fully react, break chains and decompose. The purpose of tail gas deodorization is achieved. The effect of the process of re-burning the pyrolysis oil is similar to that of direct combustion of oil sludge. Patent CN105152503 high-efficient sludge treatment system, take agitator and external heating coil's the desicator in with the nitrogen gas that nitrogen generator separated out through the conduction oil heat transfer back, with the direct convection drying of fatlute, then carry out pyrolysis and oil-water separation recovery part oil, the oil burning is the pyrolysis reactor heat supply. Only oil products in the oil sludge are removed, and the pyrolytic slag is not treated. The TPH (total petroleum hydrocarbon content) content of the treated oil sludge is lower than 1 percent. The patent CN100575285 comprehensive treatment and utilization method of ground oil sludge comprises the steps of performing solvent oil on the oil sludge in a tank cleaning process, performing secondary extraction and centrifugal separation on hot sewage to recover mineral oil, and incinerating residues. And directly incinerating the rest sludge. The residual mineral oil in the oil sludge is relatively large, and the direct incineration of the flue gas has great pollution to the environment. Solvent extraction also leaves a residual portion of the solvent in the sludge. Patent application publication No. CN106082580 is an oil sludge drying and carbonization integrated treatment zero-emission device, which is used for drying oil sludge and then burning high-temperature pyrolysis oil gas in a cyclone combustion chamber. One part of the oil sludge carbonized particles is used for filtering water and smoke in the system, and the other part of the oil sludge carbonized particles is transported outside. The pyrolysis oil gas burns together and is similar to the direct combustion effect of oil sludge, and the pollution of the combustion process to the environment cannot be avoided. In a CN106196107 harmless treatment system for oilfield sludge, oil sludge is dried and then is combusted at high temperature. The residue after incineration is not further treated and is placed as general solid waste. CN107098559 patent is an oily sludge self-heating anaerobic pyrolysis device and a pyrolysis method thereof, wherein oil sludge is pyrolyzed in a rotary pyrolysis furnace, and the product at the outlet of the pyrolysis furnace enters a direct-fired incinerator for combustion and heat supply. The process burns the pyrolysis oil together, and the generation of dioxin in the combustion process cannot be avoided. And the pyrolysed solid is not further processed. Patent CN208500715 an fatlute pyrolysis treatment device has the agitator in the adoption, and the pyrolysis oven of electrical heating carries out the pyrolysis to fatlute, and the pyrolysis sediment directly discharges, and the pyrolysis oil gas can separate out oil, and noncondensable gas gets into and fires burning furnace burning, perhaps pyrolysis oil gas direct combustion. The process pyrolyzes the sludge, but does not achieve efficient use of heat and completely harmless treatment of the sludge. Patent CN207646040 industrial continuous thermal decomposition skid-mounted equipment for sludge, which is skid-mounted equipment consisting of a feeding system, a pyrolysis system and a separation system, wherein a cracking furnace comprises a furnace body and a heating bin, the heating bin is arranged outside the furnace body, and the inside of the cracking furnace comprises a full high-temperature zone or a low-temperature zone-high-temperature zone; the cracking furnace is internally provided with a conveying chain belt. Patent CN105414155 relates to a method and apparatus for harmless treatment of petroleum industrial waste. The oil sludge is subjected to microwave heating treatment at the temperature of 500-1400 â, wherein one or a combination of more of wave-absorbing additives of graphite, silicon carbide, inorganic salt, metal and metal compound is added. This increases the yield of solid waste while treating hazardous solid waste. In patent CN108675589, a continuous oil sludge pyrolysis treatment system and a pyrolysis treatment method are disclosed, oil sludge is crushed and screened, then enters a retort furnace for dry distillation (at 650 â), pyrolysis is carried out in the pyrolysis furnace (at 700 â) and pyrolysis slag and non-condensable gas enter a combustion furnace for combustion. High-temperature flue gas generated by combustion enters the gas retort for heat supply. In the process, because the oxygen content of the flue gas is higher, the process has a certain oxidation effect on the pyrolysis oil product at high temperature, and the quality of the pyrolysis oil product cannot be ensured. In short, foreign patents mainly pyrolyze oil sludge to obtain high-quality oil products and gas, or gasify the oil sludge to obtain synthesis gas. The addition of catalyst or solvent in the treatment process can increase pollution, and the treatment process does not pay attention to whether the solid waste residue is subjected to harmless treatment. The domestic patent carries out pyrolysis on the oil sludge and recovers part of oil products. The presence of catalyst and the like added to the pyrolysis process adds additional pollution. Or the pyrolysis oil is directly combusted or is combusted again after being gasified, so that the generation of dioxin cannot be avoided, or the heat supply adopts electric heating, microwave heating and the like, which are not suitable for amplification, and the energy consumption is higher. Aiming at the defects of the prior art, the invention aims to provide a harmless treatment method for pyrolyzing oil sludge to achieve the aims of efficiently supplying heat, harmlessly treating the oil sludge and recovering oil products. The method comprises the following steps: oil sludge pretreatment, oil sludge pyrolysis, pyrolysis oil-gas separation, pyrolysis slag decarburization, heat carrier regeneration and the like. Pretreating oil sludge: and carrying out corresponding pretreatment according to the characteristics of the oil sludge. Comprising sieving, crushing, concentrating, etc. And the water and the oil separated by the oil sludge concentration enter a condensation separation system for further separation. The process reduces the water and oil content in the oil sludge and reduces the heat consumption of the pyrolysis reactor. Oil sludge pyrolysis: and (3) the pretreated oil sludge enters a pyrolyzer to be pyrolyzed under the action of a heat carrier and/or hot gas, and pyrolysis slag and pyrolysis oil gas are obtained after the oil sludge is pyrolyzed. Pyrolysis oil-gas separation: the pyrolysis oil gas is separated by a condensation separation system to obtain pyrolysis oil and pyrolysis gas, the pyrolysis gas enters a combustion system for combustion and heat supply, and the pyrolysis oil is recycled. Decarbonizing pyrolysis slag and regenerating heat carrier: and the pyrolysis gas, the pyrolysis slag and the heat carrier enter a combustion system to perform pyrolysis slag decarburization and heat carrier regeneration. The solid impurities comprise impurities such as metal, stone, woven bags and the like. Preferably, the pretreatment of the oil sludge is carried out according to the characteristics of the oil sludge, such as screening out impurities such as bulk metals, crushing, concentrating and separating water and part of oil products and the like. The oil sludge pretreatment comprises one or more of oil sludge concentration, screening, crushing, plate-frame filtration, centrifugal filtration, drum drying and the like. title: Catalysts for pyrolysis
text: Catalysts for pyrolysis Disclosed herein are processes, systems, and catalysts for improving pyrolysis technology. The disclosed processes and systems utilize a catalyst to increase pyrolysis gas (py-gas) and decrease bio-oil yields in pyrolysis reactions. The disclosed catalysts may include biochar derived from pyrolysis of industrial residuals, such as pyrolysis of wastewater biosolids (WB) and paper mill sludge (PMS). The disclosed catalysts also may include ash derived from incineration of wastewater biosolids ("biosolids incineration ash"(BIA)). Disclosed herein are processes, systems, and catalysts for improving pyrolysis technology. The disclosed processes and systems utilize a catalyst to increase pyrolysis gas (py-gas) and decrease bio-oil yields in pyrolysis reactions. The disclosed catalysts may include biochar derived from pyrolysis of industrial residuals, such as pyrolysis of wastewater biosolids (WB) and paper mill sludge (PMS). The disclosed catalysts also may include ash derived from incineration of wastewater biosolids ("biosolids incineration ash"(BIA)). [0001] The present application is a divisional application of Australian Patent Application No. 2017286813, which is the national phase of International Application No. PCT/US2017/038130, which in turn claims priority from U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/351,757, filed on June 17, 2016. The contents of each of the aforementioned applications are incorporated by cross reference in their entireties herein. [0002] The field of the invention relates to pyrolysis processes and systems. In particular, the field relates to the use of catalysts for pyrolysis processes and systems that result in increased production of pyrolysis gas (py-gas) and decreased production or elimination of bio-oil. [0003] Pyrolysis refers to the decomposition of a biomass feedstock in the absence of significant oxygen that is brought about by high temperatures. Pyrolysis processes may be characterized as "slow pyrolysis" or "fast pyrolysis." Fast pyrolysis, which is sometimes referred to as "flash pyrolysis." takes place in less than two seconds with temperatures between 300 and 550 degrees Celsius. The three main products of fast pyrolysis and slow pyrolysis are biomass char or "biochar" biomass oil or "bio-oil," and pyrolysis gas or "py gas," which includes methane, hydrogen, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and other constituents. Fast pyrolysis typically yields -60% bio-oil, -20% py-gas, and -20% biochar. Slow pyrolysis takes several minutes to hours to complete and results in biochar as the main product. [0004] Of the three main products of pyrolysis. biochar is utilized as a soil amendment for soil conditioning and carbon sequestration as well as other beneficial applications (cat litter, as a fuel, etc.). In addition, biochar derived from pyrolysis processes may be used as a catalyst in subsequent pyrolysis reactions. (See, e.g., Gilbert et al., Bioresource Technology, 100(23), 6045-6051 (2009); Sun et al., Fuel, 90(3), 1041-1048 (2011); Bosong et al., Advances in Biomedical Engineering, 9, 59, (2012); and Ren et al., RSC Advances, 4(21), 10731-10737 (2014); the contents of which are incorporated herein by reference in their entireties). [0005] The other two main products, py-gas and bio-oil, may be utilized as fuel. Py-gas is relatively clean and can be easily utilized in boilers, internal combustion engines, or other equipment for on-site energy generation. In contrast, bio-oil contains acids and water, and as such, bio-oil is corrosive and difficult to use directly as fuel. Usually, bio-oil is co-combusted with coal or natural gas at an approximately 1:9 mass ratio in boilers for energy recovery. The acidic and corrosive properties of bio-oil are always a concern because they can lead to corrosion, breakdown, and maintenance problems when used in engines. Raw bio-oil may be further processed to produce chemicals and liquid fuel, for example via catalysis, but further processing is costly and is still under development. [0006] Therefore, pyrolysis processes that result in an increase in py-gas production and/or a decrease in bio-oil yield are desirable. Here, the inventors disclose the use of catalysts that can be used in pyrolysis reactions in order to increase py-gas production and to decrease bio-oil production. [0007] Disclosed herein are processes, systems, and catalysts for improving pyrolysis technology. The present inventors have discovered that certain catalysts may be used to increase pyrolysis gas (py-gas) and decrease bio-oil in pyrolysis reactions. The disclosed catalysts may include biochar derived from pyrolysis of industrial residuals, such as pyrolysis of wastewater biosolids (WB) and paper mill sludge (PMS). The disclosed catalysts also may include ash derived from incineration of wastewater biosolids ("biosolids incineration ash" (BIA)). [0008] In one aspect, the inventors have observed that bio-chars derived from WB (WB biochar) and PMS (PMS-biochar) as well as biosolids incineration ash" (BIA) exhibit good catalytic performance in pyrolysis processes. In particular, WB-biochar, PMS-biochar, and BIA may be utilized to increase py-gas production and decrease bio-oil production in pyrolysis processes. In addition, WB-biochar, PMS-biochar, and BIA may be utilized to minimize heavy hydrocarbon content in the bio-oil. The color of condensate and bi-oil [0019] Figure 9. The catalyst temperature was maintained at the same temperature as the main reactor vessel. Dried biosolids were pyrolyzed in an oxygen-free environment by purging argon. The catalytic performance was determined by varying pyrolysis temperature and biosolids feedstock to waste-derived catalyst mass ratio. The pyrolysis temperature was varied from 500Â°C to 800Â°C; the biosolids:catalyst mass ratio ranged from 1:1 to 4:1. Blank tests without catalyst were also conducted as controls. [0085] As for bio-oil, catalyst addition resulted in a liquid product containing more low molecular weight hydrocarbons and higher water content by decomposing the tar components in the bio-oil vapor phase. Some research regarding catalytic tar reduction was published previously (Dayton, 2002; Min et al., 2011). Similarly, in this study, by converting condensable energetic hydrocarbons into gas product such as H2 and producing more water simultaneously, the bio-oil HHV decreased with the downstream catalytic upgrading. When the biosolids:catalyst mass ratio was 1:1, the HHV was lower. This indicated that energy that was originally contained in the non-catalyzed bio-oil was transferred to the gas phase via the downstream catalytic process employed. Also, the biochar HHV at three different temperatures was similar. However, the energies of the liquid and gas phases changed significantly. Bio-oil is largely composed of primary tars, a black mixture of high molecular weight hydrocarbons and free carbon. Pyrolysis vapor conversion to py-gas using catalyst has proven to be effective (Han and Kim, 2008). However, there is little information regarding catalytic wastewater biosolids pyrolysis to reduce bio-oil production. So the selection of suitable low-cost catalysts and the catalytic influence on wastewater biosolids and sludge pyrolysis should be investigated. [00171] Han, J.: Kim, H. [00308] This example describes the novel conversion of bio-oil to py-gas using inexpensive biochar derived from WB and PMS as a catalyst and using BIA as a catalyst directly. We have proven that these two biochar catalysts are surprisingly more effective than other biochars used for catalysis thus far and BIA is also effective to increase py-gas yield and reduce hio-oil yield simultaneously. Others have shown that py-gas yield can be increased and bio-oil production can he reduced during the pyrolysis of wood using biochar catalysts derived from pine wood (PW) or corn stover (CS) (Gilbert et at, 2009: Sun et al, 2011; Ren et al., 2014). However. these previous studies showed that hydrocarbons such as phenol still remained in the bio-oil Surprisingly, we discovered that WB-biochar and PMS-biochar are better biochar based catalysts due to their higher concentration of alkali metals. alkaline earth metals and other metals such as iron compared to PW-biochar and CS-biochar. BIA is also a cost-efficient catalyst because it contains high contents of calcium and iron. These three new catalysts can increase py-gas yield, decrease py-oil yield, minimize bio-oil heavy hydrocarbons to below detection limits, and have longer catalytic lifetime. The work described below was performed to evaluate the catalytic effect of WB-biochar, PMS-biochar and BIA on the pyrolysis product yield and quality. The catalytic effect of WB-biochar and PMS-biochar was compared to that of CS-biochar and PW-biochar under identical conditions. [00310] The mobile bench-scale thermochemical conversion system shown in Figure 1 was used. Dried biosolids chaff (i.e. one type of WB, the fine powder and debris originated from the wastewater biosolids drying process) was pyrolyzed in the main reactor vessel at 600Â°C to 800 0 C with the introduction of BIA catalyst in the downstream tubular reactor. where the vapor-phase passed through the catalyst bed. The biosolids chaff was from Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage District (MMSD). This chaff is similar to chaff produced at wastewater treatment plants around the world and was used to represent typical wastewater treatment plant sludge. We anticipate that results using chaff from other wastewater treatment plants will behave similarly to the results we have observed for the MMSD chaff. The tubular reactor was maintained at 600 0C to 800Â°C. The ash/chaff mass ratio varied from 0.2 to 1. Blank tests without catalyst were conducted as controls. The tubular reactor was maintained at 500Â°C for blank tests. Also, the BIA catalyst was recycled 5 times at 800Â°C with an ash/chaff mass ratio of 1 to evaluate the effectiveness over multiple cycles. 1. title: Methods and devices for pyrolysis emulsifying the continuous injection of waste synthetic resins and flammable wastes, as well as continuous discharge of pyrolysis by-products and producing high-quality without the discharge of fine dust and wastewater
text: Methods and devices for pyrolysis emulsifying the continuous injection of waste synthetic resins and flammable wastes, as well as continuous discharge of pyrolysis by-products and producing high-quality without the discharge of fine dust and wastewater The present invention relates to a pyrolysis emulsification method and apparatus for continuously inputting waste synthetic resin and combustible waste (including biowaste) as well as continuously discharging pyrolyzed by-products and producing high-quality oil without discharge of fine dust and wastewater, more preferably By continuously introducing waste synthetic resins and shredded combustible wastes (including biowaste) to a running pyrolysis device and performing pyrolysis at a constant temperature, the pyrolysis gas and carbonized by-products are continuously discharged. Because it operates without interruption, productivity is increased due to the improvement of work efficiency, and the cracks of the thermal decomposition unit due to operation interruption and thermal expansion, life extension due to aging oxidation, and wastewater are discharged by condensing and circulating the oil vapor generated in the pyrolysis unit and reusing it. By separating oil, water and gas from the pyrolysis gas generated in the pyrolysis device as well as to produce high-quality regenerated oil from the separated oil, It consists of combustible household wastes and industrial wastes as well as combustible wastes selected at landfills, removes soil, iron, etc., and crushes them, then seals and compresses them in the primary and secondary compression devices 11 and 12 to transfer screws ( 15) through the compressed transport raw material supply device 100 for transporting while blocking air and oxygen, and the compressed transported combustible waste through the compressed transport raw material supply device 100 in the gas burner 22 of the combustion chamber 21. A pyrolysis device 200 that heats with high heat to be ignited and thermally decomposes in the pyrolysis furnace 21 to transport carbonized by-products and oil vapor to the front, and the carbonized by-products separated from the pyrolysis device 200 and discharged by riding the discharge screw 31 is discharged to the lower part and the oil vapor is separated so that it can be discharged to the moving passage 41 through the filter 36, and the oil vapor separated in the separation and discharge device 300 is in contact with the cooling water to make fine The pyrolysis gas obtained by condensing and separating dust and foreign substances (tar, etc.) is transferred to the condensation separation device 400 for discharging to the gas discharge pipe 46 , and the pyrolysis gas separated by the condensation separation device 400 is transferred to the distillation column 52 . A gas-oil-water separation device 500 that separates condensed water and wastewater into water and oil in an oil-water separator 57, and a cooling circulation formed in a plurality of reduced pressure distillation tubes 61 for the pyrolysis gas transferred through the distillation column 52 A vacuum distillation device 600 that generates oil in contact with the pipe 62 and stores it in oil tanks 63, 64, and 65, and an absorption chiller by recycling heat used and discharged during thermal decomposition to generate cooling water. title: Pyrolysis to determine hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of hydrocarbon source rock
text: Pyrolysis to determine hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of hydrocarbon source rock An open system pyrolysis of a first hydrocarbon source rock sample obtained from a natural system is performed within a pyrolysis chamber by maintaining the pyrolysis chamber at a substantially constant temperature. Hydrocarbons are recovered from the pyrolysis chamber released by the first hydrocarbon source rock sample. A thermo-vaporization is performed within the pyrolysis chamber on the pyrolyzed sample at a substantially constant temperature. A first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of hydrocarbon source rock is determined. A second hydrocarbon rock sample is ground to a grain size less than or equal to or less than 250 micrometers. A second pyrolysis is performed on the ground hydrocarbon source rock sample by maintaining the chamber at a substantially constant temperature. A second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of the hydrocarbon source rock in the natural system is determined. The first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency is verified using the second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency. An open system pyrolysis of a first hydrocarbon source rock sample obtained from a natural system is performed within a pyrolysis chamber by maintaining the pyrolysis chamber at a substantially constant temperature. Hydrocarbons are recovered from the pyrolysis chamber released by the first hydrocarbon source rock sample. A thermo-vaporization is performed within the pyrolysis chamber on the pyrolyzed sample at a substantially constant temperature. A first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of hydrocarbon source rock is determined. A second hydrocarbon rock sample is ground to a grain size less than or equal to or less than 250 micrometers. A second pyrolysis is performed on the ground hydrocarbon source rock sample by maintaining the chamber at a substantially constant temperature. A second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of the hydrocarbon source rock in the natural system is determined. The first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency is verified using the second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency. This application is a divisional of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 15/637,932 filed on Jun. 29, 2017, which is a continuation-in-part of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 14/717,825 filed on May 20, 2015, both of which are incorporated by reference herein in their entirety. This specification relates to analyzing rock in which hydrocarbon is generated and trapped. Hydrocarbon exploration techniques sometimes involve generating computer-generated geological models and calibrating such models using experimental data. For example, the experimental data can be provided as inputs to the geological models. The experimental data can be obtained from laboratory experiments performed on hydrocarbon source rock, that is, rock in which hydrocarbons are generated. The accuracy of the predictions of computer-generated models can depend on the quality of the calibration of the models using measured experimental data, which, in turn, can depend on the conditions under which the laboratory experiments are performed. Said differently, the quality of the experimental data can be high if the conditions under which the laboratory experiments are performed are substantially similar to the conditions experienced by the rock in the subsurface from which the hydrocarbons are produced. One input to the geological model can include a characteristic of the hydrocarbon rock to expel trapped hydrocarbons. Pyrolysis is one technique to study the characteristic of hydrocarbon source rock to expel or trap hydrocarbons. This specification describes pyrolysis techniques to analyze the characteristics of a hydrocarbon source rock to expel/retain trapped hydrocarbons. In particular, for example, this specification describes pyrolysis to determine hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of hydrocarbon source rock. An example implementation of the subject matter described within this disclosure is a method with the following features. An open system pyrolysis of a first hydrocarbon source rock sample obtained from a natural system is performed within a pyrolysis chamber resulting in a pyrolyzed sample. The open system pyrolysis is performed by maintaining the pyrolysis chamber at a substantially constant temperature of 375Â° C. The first hydrocarbon source rock sample includes hydrocarbon source rocks having an equivalent spherical diameter of substantially at least one centimeter. Hydrocarbons are recovered from the pyrolysis chamber released by the first hydrocarbon source rock sample in response to the open system pyrolysis. A thermo-vaporization is performed within the pyrolysis chamber on the pyrolyzed sample on which the open system pyrolysis was performed at a substantially constant temperature of 375Â° C. Hydrocarbons released by the pyrolyzed sample in response to the thermo-vaporization are recovered from the pyrolysis chamber. A first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of hydrocarbon source rock in the natural system is determined based on the recovered hydrocarbons released by the first hydrocarbon source rock sample in response to the open system pyrolysis and based on the recovered hydrocarbons released by the pyrolyzed sample in response to thermo-vaporization. A second hydrocarbon rock sample of a pre-defined mass is ground resulting in a ground hydrocarbon source rock sample having a grain size less than or equal to or less than 250 micrometers. The grinding is performed within an integrated sample-crusher and thermo-vaporization chamber. A second pyrolysis is performed within the integrated sample-crusher and thermo-vaporization chamber on the ground hydrocarbon source rock sample. The second pyrolysis is performed by maintaining the integrated sample-crusher and thermo-vaporization chamber at a substantially constant temperature of 375Â° C. within the integrated sample-crusher and thermo-vaporization chamber. A second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of the hydrocarbon source rock in the natural system is determined based on performing the second pyrolysis on the second hydrocarbon source rock sample. The first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency is verified using the second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency. An example implementation of the subject matter described within this disclosure is a second method with the following features. An open system pyrolysis is performed within a pyrolysis chamber on a hydrocarbon source rock sample that includes fragments having an equivalent spherical diameter of substantially at least one centimeter. Performing the open system pyrolysis results in a pyrolyzed rock sample. Hydrocarbons released by the rock sample in response to the open system pyrolysis are recovered. A first quantity of hydrocarbons released in response to the open system pyrolysis is determined. A thermo-vaporization is performed within the pyrolysis chamber on the pyrolyzed rock sample. Hydrocarbons released by the rock sample in the pyrolysis chamber in response to the thermo-vaporization are recovered. A second quantity of hydrocarbons released in response to thermo-vaporization in the pyrolysis chamber is determined. The sample are placed in a crushing chamber and crushing and performing thermo-vaporization on the pyrolyzed rock sample. Hydrocarbons released by the rock sample in response to crushing and thermo-vaporization are recovered. A third quantity of hydrocarbons released in response to crushing and thermo-vaporization in the crushing chamber is determined. A first hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of the hydrocarbon source rock is determined as a ratio of a sum of the first quantity of hydrocarbons to a sum of the first quantity of hydrocarbons, the second quantity of hydrocarbons, and the third quantity of hydrocarbons. A powdered sample of the hydrocarbon source rock having a grain size less than or equal to substantially 250 microns is pyrolyzed. A fourth quantity of hydrocarbons released in response to performing open system pyrolysis on a powdered sample is determined. A second hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency of the hydrocarbon source rock is determined as a ratio of the first quantity of hydrocarbons to the fourth quantity of hydrocarbons. The hydrocarbon expulsion efficiency is provided as an input to a geological model capable of analyzing a hydrocarbon expulsion from the hydrocarbon source rock through geological history.
